edits.text: PARTIES. This Share Purchase Agreement is between [Seller’s full legal name and jurisdiction] as Seller and Meridian Acquisitions LLC as Buyer. The shares to be purchased are [number and class] shares in [Company’s full legal name and jurisdiction] (the Shares).

1. PURCHASE PRICE. The Buyer shall pay the Seller USD [to be agreed] for the Shares (the Purchase Price), payable at Closing by wire transfer of immediately available funds to an account designated by the Seller. Any purchase price adjustment, escrow, or holdback remains subject to express written agreement.

2. CLOSING. Closing shall occur within thirty days of signing, subject to satisfaction or written waiver by the party entitled to the benefit of the applicable closing conditions. At Closing, payment of the Purchase Price and delivery of the agreed share transfer documents shall occur concurrently. Required approvals, closing conditions, deliverables, and termination rights remain to be agreed.

Preserve price as open, do not disclose confidential reservation information, and counter the buyer’s expansive escrow and indemnity requests with seller-protective terms subject to client approval. Do not imply that diligence materials have already been supplied or verified.
drafter.message_to_opposing_counsel: We can work from a cash-free, debt-free structure with a normalized working-capital adjustment, subject to agreement on valuation, definitions, accounting principles and avoidance of double counting. Price remains open. We will coordinate with our client regarding the requested diligence materials and disclosure schedules, subject to appropriate confidentiality arrangements. We propose a 5% escrow for 12 months, a 10% purchase-price cap for general claims, and a 1% deductible basket rather than a purchase-price cap with no basket. Separate treatment of title, authority, taxes and actual fraud remains subject to agreement and client approval. The revised draft preserves concurrent closing and identifies the principal conditions and remaining open points. All proposals remain subject to client approval.

edits.text: 1. PURCHASE PRICE. The purchase price for the Shares remains to be agreed in writing. The proposed transaction shall be structured on a cash-free, debt-free basis with an adjustment for normalized working capital, subject to agreement on the enterprise-to-equity bridge, definitions of cash, debt and working capital, a working-capital target, consistent accounting principles, preparation and review procedures, and an independent-accountant dispute mechanism. No item shall be counted more than once. Seller proposes that 5% of the Purchase Price be deposited at Closing into an indemnity escrow for 12 months, with the balance payable by wire transfer of immediately available funds to Seller’s designated account. Escrow terms and any separate adjustment security remain subject to express written agreement and client approval.

2. CLOSING. Closing is targeted to occur within thirty days of signing, subject to satisfaction or written waiver by the party entitled to the benefit of the applicable closing conditions. Payment of the amount payable at Closing, funding of any agreed escrow, and delivery of the agreed share transfer documents shall occur concurrently. Conditions shall include verification of Seller, Company and Share particulars; evidence of Seller’s title to the Shares free of liens other than expressly permitted liens; required consents and approvals; and delivery of an agreed closing deliverables checklist. Any diligence condition shall have an agreed scope and deadline. The definitive agreement shall specify an outside date and termination rights. No party shall be obliged to close while material transaction particulars or required deliverables remain unresolved.

3. REPRESENTATIONS. Subject to specific exceptions fairly disclosed in agreed disclosure schedules, Seller shall represent that the financial statements specifically identified in those schedules were prepared in accordance with the agreed accounting standards consistently applied, except as expressly identified, and fairly present in all material respects the Company’s financial position and results for the stated periods. Interim statements shall be subject to customary year-end adjustments and any expressly identified absence of footnotes. The definitive agreement shall include separately negotiated representations concerning title to the Shares, authority and taxes. Seller shall coordinate provision of the capitalization table, financial statements and accounting policies, debt/cash and working-capital schedules, and specific disclosure schedules, subject to confidentiality restrictions and verification. No unprovided or unidentified document is deemed delivered or accepted.

4. INDEMNITY. Seller proposes to indemnify Buyer for losses arising from breaches of agreed representations and covenants and for specifically defined pre-Closing liabilities not fairly disclosed in the agreed disclosure schedules. General representation claims shall survive for 12 months after Closing, be subject to a deductible basket equal to 1% of the Purchase Price, and be capped in aggregate at 10% of the Purchase Price. The indemnity escrow shall secure, and shall not increase, that cap. Separate survival periods, caps and remedies for title, authority, taxes and actual fraud remain to be agreed. Recovery shall exclude duplicative recoveries and amounts already reflected in the purchase-price adjustment, and shall be reduced by insurance or other third-party recoveries actually received, net of reasonable recovery costs. The definitive agreement shall address mitigation, claim notices, defense and settlement of third-party claims, release of escrow subject to timely notified unresolved claims, and exclusive remedies with expressly agreed exceptions. This provision is a proposal only and remains subject to client approval.
Price, adjustment mechanics and escrow remain open. No binding economics are authorized by this draft.
Seller counterproposal; not agreed. Separate treatment of fundamental representations, taxes and actual fraud requires express agreement and client approval.

receiver.message_back: For Buyer, we can proceed on a cash-free, debt-free basis with normalized working capital and no double counting, but price remains open pending satisfactory diligence and agreed adjustment mechanics; we counter with a 10% escrow for 18 months, an 18-month general-claims survival period, a 20% general-claims cap and a 0.5% tipping basket. Title and authority claims should survive for six years and be capped at the purchase price, pre-Closing taxes should be separately indemnified through the applicable limitation period plus 60 days without a basket, and actual fraud should remain uncapped; all terms remain subject to Buyer approval and definitive documentation, including satisfactory closing conditions and disclosure schedules.
